les: Vyf maniere om kos te kry
kaps_punt: Maniere waarop mense hul voedsel verkry - koop; verbou; versamel, visvang, jag

items.bewering: Elke mens het elke dag kos nodig, maar nie almal kry hul kos op dieselfde manier nie.
items.bron: The Conversation, 'Curious Kids: why do we need food?' (theconversation.com/curious-kids-why-do-we-need-food-98938); KidsHealth (kidshealth.org/en/kids/calorie.html): the body uses energy all the time, even asleep, and energy stores are not kept long, so food has to be eaten regularly. The universal 'elke mens ... elke dag' is the ordinary nutritional statement (a person can survive some days without food, but needs it daily to stay healthy), which is how a Grade 4 learner will read it. Checked in full this round.

items.bewering: Daar is vyf belangrike maniere waarop mense aan kos kom. Hulle koop dit, of hulle verbou dit self. Hulle kan dit ook versamel, vis vang of jag.
items.bron: Each of the five is an attested way South Africans obtain food: buying (Stats SA GHS 2023, see 'Koop'), own crops (GHS 2023 Table 18.1), gathering wild leafy vegetables (Jansen van Rensburg et al. 2007, 'African leafy vegetables in South Africa', Water SA, repository.up.ac.za/handle/2263/4875), fishing (FAO country profile FI_CP_ZA) and hunting (Univ. of Pretoria, 'Jobs, game meat and profits', repository.up.ac.za). 'Vyf belangrike maniere' does not claim the list is complete, so it is not false that other routes exist (school feeding, gifts, keeping animals). Checked in full this round.

items.bewering: Die meeste mense in Suid-Afrika koop hul kos by 'n winkel.
items.bron: Stats SA, General Household Survey 2023 (P0318), section 18, pp. 65-66: only 17,4% of households were involved in any agricultural production, and of those only 11,7% named it their main source of food (about 2% of all households); 75,5% did it for an EXTRA source of food. So the great majority of households get their food mainly by buying it. Checked in full this round.

items.bewering: Die winkel koop die kos weer by boere en ander mense wat kos maak.
items.bron: NAMC Food Price Monitoring Report 2004, 'Food value chains: wheat' (namc.co.za): the chain runs from farmers through millers and bakers to retailers. Shops also buy through wholesalers and distributors, which this simplification leaves out; leaving them out does not make it false. Checked in full this round.

items.bewering: Dink aan 'n brood op die winkelrak. Die winkel het die brood by 'n bakkery gekoop. Die bakker het dit van meel gebak. Die meel kom van koring wat 'n boer geplant het.
items.bron: NAMC 2004 wheat value-chain report (namc.co.za/wp-content/uploads/2017/09/FPM-Report-2004_04_03_FoodValueChains_Wheat.pdf): farmer -> silo -> miller (flour) -> baker -> retailer; Minister Didiza, National Chamber of Milling AGM (gov.za): bread and cake flour comes from milled wheat. Each step stated is true. The mill between wheat and flour is skipped but 'die meel kom van koring' remains true. About half of SA's wheat is imported (a dtic case study, as reported in the search results), but it is still wheat a farmer planted, so the sentence holds. Some supermarkets bake in-store; as one worked example this is not a falsehood. Checked in full this round.

items.bewering: So begin baie van die kos wat ons koop, by 'n boer.
items.bron: NAMC 2004 food value-chain report (namc.co.za): food value chains start with agricultural production. 'Baie' rather than 'alle' is correctly narrow (sea fish, for example, do not start with a farmer). Checked in full this round.

items.bewering: Verbou beteken dat jy die kos self kweek. Hulle plant groente, vrugte of kruie in 'n tuin en gee dit water. By verbou plant die mens self die plante in die grond en sorg vir hulle tot hulle kos gee.
items.bron: Stats SA GHS 2023, Table 18.1 (p. 66): of households engaged in agriculture, 58,9% grew fruit and vegetables and 47,1% grains and food crops. weet.co.za, 'Gewasboerdery in Suid-Afrika' (an Afrikaans reference page, not a textbook): crops ('gewasse') are kinds of plants that are 'verbou'. The meaning given (planting and tending plants until they produce food) matches. Checked in full this round.

items.bewering: Party gesinne hou ook self hoenders aan vir eiers of 'n koei vir melk.
items.bron: Stats SA GHS 2023, Table 18.1 (p. 66): 36,6% of agricultural households produced poultry and 26,2% livestock. True as a statement about South African families. Its PLACEMENT is raised as a separate item below. Checked in full this round.

items.bewering: [Classification implied by placement] The sentence about families keeping hens for eggs or a cow for milk sits inside the 'Verbou' block, straight after the definition 'By verbou plant die mens self die plante in die grond'. A learner sorting 'eggs from our own hens' into the lesson's five ways will put it under verbou.
items.bron: The lesson defines verbou only in terms of plants ('plant ... die plante in die grond en sorg vir hulle tot hulle kos gee'; summary block: 'Jy kweek die kos self wanneer jy verbou'). Afrikaans agricultural usage separates 'gewasboerdery' (crops, which are 'verbou') from 'veeteelt/veeboerdery' (animals) (weet.co.za, 'Gewasboerdery in Suid-Afrika'), and Stats SA also lists poultry and livestock separately from crops (GHS 2023, Table 18.1). That suggests keeping animals is not 'verbou'. But I could not reach an authoritative Afrikaans dictionary entry for 'verbou' (WAT online needs a login; other dictionary pages returned 404). Also, in English, 'growing your own food' is often used loosely to include backyard hens. None of the five named ways clearly covers keeping animals, so this is partly about how the curriculum scheme is applied, not only about facts. A person should decide whether to (a) keep the sentence but make clear that keeping animals is a different way of producing your own food, not verbou; (b) remove it; or (c) accept the looser reading. The lesson's own definition argues against (c). Checked this round; not resolved.

items.bewering: Versamel is anders as verbou. 'n Kosversamelaar plant niks nie maar haal kos wat reeds in die natuur groei. Dit kan wilde blare of vrugte wees wat vanself in die veld groei.
items.bron: Jansen van Rensburg et al. 2007, 'African leafy vegetables in South Africa', Water SA (repository.up.ac.za/handle/2263/4875): morogo/imifino is collected wild or from fields where it grows as a weed, and is still commonly used in poor rural areas. Farmer's Weekly, 'Imifino – traditional food with a future' (farmersweekly.co.za). Gathering wild fruit is the same kind of activity. Checked in full this round.

items.bewering: Sommige plante, bessies en sampioene is giftig.
items.bron: Western Cape Department of Health warning on death cap (Amanita phalloides) poisoning, July 2026, reported by False Bay Echo / Sentinel News (falsebayecho.co.za, 2026-07-07); UCT Faculty of Health Sciences document on poisonous fungi (health.uct.ac.za/node/149857); St Olaf College Natural Lands, 'Poisonous berries of Minnesota' (wp.stolaf.edu/naturallands/poisonous-berries-of-minnesota). Listing mushrooms separately from plants is correct, since mushrooms are fungi. Checked in full this round.

items.bewering: Dit beteken dat hulle mense of diere siek kan maak of skade kan doen as hulle in die liggaam kom, soos wanneer hulle geëet word.
items.bron: MeSH (US National Library of Medicine), 'Poisons': substances that, when ingested, inhaled or absorbed, can damage body structures or disturb how they work; GEMET (eionet.europa.eu/gemet/concept/6358), the same. 'Soos wanneer hulle geëet word' is correctly given as one example of a way in, not the only one. Checked in full this round.

items.bewering: 'n Giftige bessie kan amper net so lyk soos een wat veilig is. Daarom moet iemand wat kos versamel, die plante baie goed ken.
items.bron: St Olaf College Natural Lands, 'Poisonous berries of Minnesota' (lists look-alikes for each species); Outdoor Life, 'Identify toxic plants that look like food'. For South Africa, the Western Cape Health warning (July 2026, via falsebayecho.co.za) says death cap looks like edible mushrooms and you cannot tell it is safe from how it looks; foragers are told to go with an expert. The comparison between a poisonous and a safe berry is a factual look-alike claim and holds. Checked in full this round.

items.bewering: Mense vang ook vis vir kos. Party vang vis in die see met 'n hengel van die rotse af.
items.bron: Rhodes University research repository, 'An assessment of the shore baitfishery in the Eastern Cape' (researchrepository.ru.ac.za/handle/20.500.14915/4995); survey of the recreational rock-angling fishery at Port Elizabeth (figshare.utas.edu.au/articles/journal_contribution/22863440); City of Cape Town, 'Ocean fishing' (capetown.gov.za). Rock angling with a rod is a well-established fishery in South Africa. Checked in full this round.

items.bewering: Ander gaan met 'n boot uit en vang vis met nette.
items.bron: FAO Fishery Country Profile, South Africa (fao.org/fishery/docs/DOCUMENT/fcp/en/FI_CP_ZA.pdf): the offshore industrial sector is dominated by the purse-seine fishery for sardine and anchovy and by hake trawling. Marine Living Resources Act 18 of 1998, definitions: a purse-seine is an encircling net. Some boats fish with lines, but 'ander' does not claim all boats use nets. Checked in full this round.

items.bewering: Mense vang ook vis in riviere en damme. Daar is die water gewoonlik varswater, wat baie min sout bevat.
items.bron: USGS Water Science School, 'Saline water use in the United States' (usgs.gov): fresh water is defined as having less than 1 000 ppm of dissolved salts, so 'baie min sout' is accurate. 'Gewoonlik' rightly allows for estuaries and some brackish inland water. Wikipedia, 'Smallmouth yellowfish' and 'Boskop Dam': people angle for yellowfish, bass, carp and catfish in South African rivers (Vaal, Orange) and dams. Checked in full this round.

items.bewering: Sommige mense jag ook wilde diere vir hul vleis.
items.bron: University of Pretoria repository, 'Jobs, game meat and profits: the benefits of wildlife ranching on marginal lands in South Africa' (repository.up.ac.za/items/1428dd64-c946-46e4-a652-03a6f617e1d4); Farmer's Weekly, 'New book explores game ranch profitability in SA': an estimated 200 000 local biltong hunters, i.e. hunting for meat. Checked in full this round.

items.bewering: Versamel, visvang en jag haal kos direk uit die natuur.
items.blok: Uit die natuur of by die winkel
items.bron: Same sources as the gathering, fishing and hunting items above (Water SA 2007; FAO FI_CP_ZA; UP wildlife-ranching study). All three take wild plants or animals that people did not raise. Biltong hunting is often on game farms where the game is managed, but the animals are still wild animals in the veld, so 'uit die natuur' holds at Grade 4 level. Checked in full this round.

items.bewering: Jy kweek die kos self wanneer jy verbou. Iemand anders het dit gewoonlik eers vir jou gekweek of gevang wanneer jy koop.
items.blok: Uit die natuur of by die winkel
items.bron: NAMC 2004 food value-chain report (namc.co.za): food sold in shops comes from farmers (grown) or from fisheries (caught) through processors. 'Gewoonlik' covers exceptions such as salt. Checked in full this round. NOTE: 'Jy kweek die kos self wanneer jy verbou' bears on the open item about hens in the 'Verbou' block.

items.bewering: Die meeste mense in Suid-Afrika kry hul kos deur dit te koop.
items.blok: Uit die natuur of by die winkel
items.bron: Stats SA, General Household Survey 2023 (P0318), pp. 65-66: 17,4% of households do any agriculture and 11,7% of those use it as their main food source (about 2% of all households), so most households rely on bought food. This is consistent with the same claim in 'Koop'. Checked in full this round.

items.bewering: kosversamelaar: Iemand wat kos haal wat vanself in die natuur groei, soos wilde blare en vrugte.
items.bron: Matches the gathering practice described in Jansen van Rensburg et al. 2007, Water SA (repository.up.ac.za/handle/2263/4875): wild leafy vegetables collected where they grow by themselves. It is accurate read on its own, outside the block, and agrees with the 'Versamel' block. Checked in full this round.

items.bewering: giftig: Iets wat mense of diere siek kan maak of skade kan doen as dit in die liggaam kom, soos wanneer dit geëet word.
items.bron: MeSH 'Poisons' (US National Library of Medicine) and GEMET concept 6358 (eionet.europa.eu): harm or illness from a substance that gets into the body by being swallowed, breathed in or absorbed. Eating is given correctly as one example. It is accurate read on its own and identical in substance to the sentence in 'Versamel'. Checked in full this round.

opsomming: Every factual claim checks out against Stats SA, university, FAO and health-department sources, including both 'die meeste mense koop hul kos' claims (only about 2% of households rely mainly on growing their own food) and the bread chain. A person needs to decide one thing: the sentence about families keeping hens for eggs or a cow for milk is true, but it sits in the 'Verbou' block, where the lesson defines verbou as planting plants and Afrikaans usage separates crops from livestock. A learner will therefore file keeping animals under verbou. I could not reach a dictionary to settle whether that is wrong, so a person should choose between making the difference explicit, cutting the sentence, or accepting the looser reading. The lesson contains no analogies; the one comparison (a poisonous berry can look like a safe one) is factual and holds.
